>1) How you expect "good use of technique" to prevent computers more intelligent than humans from being developed, or, if they are developed, how you expect them to also prevent said
>computers from supplanting humans.
The same way tech is controlled now: legislation.
>(2) how you expect "good use of technique" to avoid the risk of biological disaster that biotechnological experimentation entails.
I don’t. I accept managed risk. I would say the anti-tech position is no less risky, given the exposure to such a cruel mother as nature.
>(3) how you expect "good use of technique" to prevent the progressive lowering of standards of human dignity that we’ve been seeing at least since the early stages of the Industrial Revolution.
I don’t accept the human dignity has been lowered. This is what I mean by having a skewed perspective on things.
>(4) how you expect "good use of technique" to bring nuclear weapons under control.
We already have for almost a century now.
>You've mentioned also "The only reason technique exists because it is efficient at producing a certain good" and that may be true, Dr Kaczynski does mention that there are two kinds of technology, one that is used in small scale communities and another that is used in large scale social organizations. for more about this i'll have to refer you to "Technological Slavery" and "Anti tech revolution: Why and How".
What is the point of making this distinction of scale? Are you saying the scale of the technique is inversely proportional to its negative affects on humanity? I don’t really think you can make such broad statements like that."}]
